:::: {.columns .faust-layout}
::: {.column width="50%" .add-space}
::: {style="font-size: 90%;"}
::: {style="opacity: 0.5"}
- **Modulation** in audio DSP is the process of ***using signals*** to **drive** or ***influence other signal parameters*** (such as *frequency*, *amplitude*, *phase*, etc.).
- In order to do so, ***low-frequency signals*** are often used: **envelope generators**, **low-frequency oscillators** (**LFOs**) or **noise/random generators**, etc.
:::
- **Amplitude modulation** can be used to **shape the envelope of a signal**, or to create the *ring-modulation* effect.
:::
:::

## Faust: Modulation {auto-animate=true}
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

:::: {.columns .faust-layout}
::: {.column width="50%" .add-space}
::: {style="font-size: 90%;"}
::: {style="opacity: 0.5"}
- **Modulation** in audio DSP is the process of ***using signals*** to **drive** or ***influence other signal parameters*** (such as *frequency*, *amplitude*, *phase*, etc.).
- In order to do so, ***low-frequency signals*** are often used: **envelope generators**, **low-frequency oscillators** (**LFOs**) or **noise/random generators**, etc.
- **Amplitude modulation** can be used to **shape the envelope of a signal**, or to create the *ring-modulation* effect.
:::
- **Envelope generators** are often presented as **AR** (*attack*/*release*) or **ADSR** (*attack*/*decay*/*sustain*/*release*) envelopes. They can be also used to modulate other parameters (such as a *filter's cutoff frequency*).
:::
:::

::: {.column width="44%"}
```{.js code-line-numbers="" filename="faust/examples/modulation-3.dsp"}
{{< include /faust/examples/modulation-3.dsp >}}
```
{{< faust faust/examples/modulation-3.dsp >}}
:::

- Finally, **noise generators** can introduce *randomness* in modulation, which can be useful for **generative patches** or *sound installations*, etc.
:::
